title: Classical regularity and attainment in portfolio choice with nonhomothetic utility
summary: We study classical regularity and attainment in terminal-utility portfolio choice with unspanned factors, nonnegative wealth, and exposures that are square-integrable in expectation. A joint estimate for logarithmic marginal utility controls relative risk aversion and factor sensitivity. In several dimensions, a risk-price component uniformly separated from the factor-hedging span gives classical solvability and a unique strong optimal portfolio on every finite horizon.
